options: Copies the server to your laptop
Opens an encrypted terminal on bazaar-server, logged in as the user asha
questions.explain: asha is the user on the server; bazaar-server is the machine. Everything you type travels encrypted.

questions.q: The first connection asks "Are you sure you want to continue connecting?". What is SSH protecting you from?
options: Talking to an impostor pretending to be your server
questions.explain: After yes, the server's ID is saved in known_hosts. If it ever changes, SSH warns loudly.

questions.q: Which file may you copy to every server you want to log in to?
questions.explain: The .pub file is the public key. The private key (without .pub) must never leave your laptop.

questions.q: Which two commands set up key login?
questions.explain: ssh-keygen makes the key pair; ssh-copy-id adds the public key to the server's authorized_keys.

questions.q: SSH says "WARNING: UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE! Permissions 0644 ... are too open". What's the fix?
questions.explain: A private key must be readable only by you. SSH ignores it otherwise.

questions.q: How do you copy order_20261121.log from the server to the current folder on your laptop?
questions.explain: scp works like cp, with one side written as user@server:path. The . means here.

questions.q: (Going deeper) During a key login, what does the laptop send to the server?
options: A signature of the server's random challenge, made with the private key
questions.explain: The server checks the signature with the public key. The private key never leaves the laptop.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why set PasswordAuthentication no on a real server, and what must you check first?
options: It makes SSH faster; nothing to check
Password guessing becomes useless; first make sure your key login works, with a second session open
questions.explain: Otherwise you can lock yourself out of your own server.
